memory_update.text: STRL appears to be the most node-pure public candidate found in this pass because it explicitly combines data-center site development and mission-critical electrical services, with 2025 growth driven by higher data-center volume.

EME and FIX are direct construction-capacity candidates; both need margin-quality checks because data-center backlog can still fail the Serenity test if projects convert into low-margin or delayed work.

PWR is a second-order grid/interconnection candidate rather than a site builder; include in this node because power availability and utility construction often determine whether permitted data-center sites can be energized.

ACM is a permitting/environmental/planning hypothesis candidate; direct AI revenue sensitivity is less proven than for contractors, but its service menu aligns with local-regulatory, water, power and environmental bottlenecks.

Need a separate pass for private or non-US-listed data-center builders and EPCs such as DPR, Turner, Mortenson, Burns & McDonnell, Holder, Black & Veatch, Clayco and PowerHouse because many chokepoint leaders are not straightforward US-listed equities.

Need a regulated-utility docket pass to map site-specific interconnection, special-rate contracts, ratepayer-protection conditions, water-service moratoria and tax-incentive records to listed utilities and contractors.

node: Data-center land, construction, EPC, permitting, water and local-regulatory capacity
summary: Expanded universe for the site-control/construction/permitting node favors specialty contractors and infrastructure consultants rather than chip or cloud names. The strongest direct public-market mappings found in this pass are electrical/mechanical contractors, site-development contractors, grid-construction contractors, and permitting/environmental-advisory firms. Key chokepoint logic: AI data-center demand is translating into large backlogs, but realization depends on labor availability, equipment delivery, customer permitting, power interconnection, water/cooling approvals, local politics, and profitable execution.
